questions.stem: A 47-year-old man is found to have high blood pressure at a work screening. He has mild muscle cramps. Blood pressure is 168/100 mm Hg. Jugular venous pressure is normal, and there is no edema. Laboratory studies show: sodium 143 mEq/L (normal 135-145), potassium 2.9 mEq/L (normal 3.5-5.0), bicarbonate 31 mEq/L (normal 22-28), plasma renin activity 0.2 ng/mL/h (normal 0.5-4.0) and plasma aldosterone 38 ng/dL (normal 4-31). CT shows a 1.5-cm nodule in the left adrenal gland. Which mechanism best explains why he has no edema despite ongoing aldosterone excess?
choices: Loss of mineralocorticoid receptors from the principal cells of the collecting duct
Pressure natriuresis and natriuretic peptides that offset sodium retention
Hypokalemia that blunts the effect of aldosterone on ENaC channels
Water loss from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus caused by hypokalemia
Metabolic alkalosis that closes ENaC channels in the collecting duct
questions.explanation: In primary hyperaldosteronism, sodium is retained only at first. The larger plasma volume raises renal perfusion pressure (**pressure natriuresis**) and stretches the atria (more **ANP**), so other nephron segments excrete more sodium: this is **aldosterone escape**, and edema does not form. Potassium and H+ secretion do not escape, so **hypokalemia** and **metabolic alkalosis** persist. Hypokalemia can cause a mild nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, but losing free water does not stop the sodium retention that would cause edema.
questions.explanation_pt: No hiperaldosteronismo primário, o sódio é retido apenas no início. O maior volume plasmático eleva a pressão de perfusão renal (**natriurese pressórica**) e distende os átrios (mais **peptídeo natriurético atrial**), de modo que outros segmentos do néfron excretam mais sódio: é o **escape da aldosterona**, e não se forma edema. A secreção de potássio e de H+ não escapa, então a **hipocalemia** e a **alcalose metabólica** persistem. A hipocalemia pode causar um diabetes insípido nefrogênico leve, mas perder água livre não impede a retenção de sódio que causaria edema.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had 3 weeks of muscle weakness and new high blood pressure. To help her stop smoking, she recently began eating a large amount of black licorice candy every day. She takes no medications. Blood pressure is 164/98 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show: potassium 2.7 mEq/L (normal 3.5-5.0); bicarbonate 32 mEq/L (normal 22-28); plasma renin activity low; plasma aldosterone low; morning serum cortisol normal. Which mechanism best explains her findings?
choices: Inherited gain-of-function mutation that keeps ENaC channels in the apical membrane
Inhibition of renal 11β-HSD2, so cortisol stimulates mineralocorticoid receptors
Autonomous aldosterone secretion by a small adrenocortical adenoma in the zona glomerulosa
Inhibition of adrenal 11β-hydroxylase, with buildup of 11-deoxycorticosterone
Increased renin release from juxtaglomerular cells, with secondary aldosteronism
questions.explanation: **Glycyrrhetinic acid** in licorice inhibits **11β-HSD2**, the enzyme in the collecting duct that turns cortisol into inactive cortisone. Cortisol, which circulates at much higher levels than aldosterone, then binds **mineralocorticoid receptors** and causes sodium retention, **hypertension**, **hypokalemia** and **metabolic alkalosis**, with **low renin and low aldosterone** (apparent mineralocorticoid excess). An adenoma or a renin-driven process would make aldosterone high, not low, and Liddle syndrome is inherited, not caused by a new food. 11β-hydroxylase inhibition also lowers renin and aldosterone, but it lowers cortisol, while her cortisol is normal and her problem began with the licorice.
questions.explanation_pt: O **ácido glicirretínico** do alcaçuz inibe a **11β-HSD2**, a enzima do ducto coletor que transforma o cortisol em cortisona inativa. O cortisol, que circula em níveis muito maiores que a aldosterona, passa então a se ligar aos **receptores mineralocorticoides** e causa retenção de sódio, **hipertensão**, **hipocalemia** e **alcalose metabólica**, com **renina e aldosterona baixas** (excesso aparente de mineralocorticoide). Um adenoma ou um processo mediado por renina deixaria a aldosterona alta, e não baixa, e a síndrome de Liddle é hereditária, e não causada por um alimento novo. A inibição da 11β-hidroxilase também reduz a renina e a aldosterona, mas reduz o cortisol, e o cortisol dela está normal e o quadro começou com o alcaçuz.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has had 5 months of weight gain, a fuller face, acne, a deeper voice and thinning scalp hair. She now shaves her chin, and her menstrual periods stopped 3 months ago. She takes no medications. Blood pressure is 162/98 mm Hg. She has purple abdominal striae and an enlarged clitoris. Laboratory studies show: 24-hour urinary free cortisol four times the upper limit of normal; plasma ACTH below 5 pg/mL (normal 10-60); DHEA sulfate 1,450 μg/dL (normal 35-430); total testosterone high. CT shows an irregular 10-cm left adrenal mass with areas of necrosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
choices: Adrenocortical carcinoma
Cortisol-secreting adrenocortical adenoma
ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma
Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor of the ovary
Nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency
questions.explanation: Fast-onset **cortisol excess together with virilization**, a suppressed ACTH and a very high **DHEA sulfate** (an androgen made almost only by the adrenal) point to an adrenal tumor that makes several steroids. A large, irregular, necrotic mass fits **adrenocortical carcinoma**. A benign cortisol-secreting adenoma is usually small and makes cortisol alone, so it rarely causes marked virilization. A Sertoli-Leydig tumor raises testosterone but not DHEA sulfate or cortisol, a pituitary adenoma would raise ACTH, and nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes mild androgen excess but no cortisol excess.
questions.explanation_pt: **Excesso de cortisol com virilização** de início rápido, ACTH suprimido e **sulfato de DHEA** muito alto (um andrógeno produzido quase só pela adrenal) indicam um tumor adrenal que produz vários esteroides. Uma massa grande, irregular e necrótica corresponde a **carcinoma adrenocortical**. Um adenoma benigno secretor de cortisol geralmente é pequeno e produz só cortisol, por isso raramente causa virilização importante. O tumor de Sertoli-Leydig eleva a testosterona, mas não o sulfato de DHEA nem o cortisol, um adenoma hipofisário elevaria o ACTH, e a deficiência não clássica de 21-hidroxilase causa excesso leve de andrógenos, mas não excesso de cortisol.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because she has not had a menstrual period. She has no breast development and no pubic or axillary hair. Her external genitalia are normal female. Blood pressure is 156/96 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show: potassium 3.0 mEq/L (normal 3.5-5.0); morning cortisol low; ACTH high; plasma renin activity low; aldosterone low; LH and FSH high; estradiol very low. Karyotype is 46,XX, and pelvic ultrasound shows a small uterus and two ovaries. Deficiency of which enzyme best explains her findings?
choices: 21-hydroxylase
11β-hydroxylase
3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
Aromatase
17α-hydroxylase
questions.explanation: **17α-hydroxylase** is needed to make cortisol and all **sex steroids** in both the adrenals and the gonads. Without it, there is no estrogen at puberty (absent breasts, high LH and FSH) and no adrenal androgens (no pubic hair). High ACTH pushes precursors into the mineralocorticoid branch, so excess **11-deoxycorticosterone** causes **hypertension**, **hypokalemia** and **low renin and aldosterone**. 11β-hydroxylase deficiency also causes hypertension with low renin, but its extra androgens would cause early pubic hair and virilization, not sexual infantilism, and aromatase deficiency virilizes a 46,XX baby at birth without hypertension.
questions.explanation_pt: A **17α-hidroxilase** é necessária para produzir cortisol e todos os **esteroides sexuais**, nas adrenais e nas gônadas. Sem ela, não há estrogênio na puberdade (mamas ausentes, LH e FSH altos) nem andrógenos adrenais (sem pelos pubianos). O ACTH alto desvia os precursores para a via mineralocorticoide, e o excesso de **11-desoxicorticosterona** causa **hipertensão**, **hipocalemia** e **renina e aldosterona baixas**. A deficiência de 11β-hidroxilase também causa hipertensão com renina baixa, mas o excesso de andrógenos causaria pelos pubianos precoces e virilização, e não infantilismo sexual, e a deficiência de aromatase viriliza a recém-nascida 46,XX, sem hipertensão.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with a pounding headache, sweating and palpitations. She has had similar short attacks for 4 months. Blood pressure is 176/104 mm Hg, and pulse is 128/min. She is given intravenous propranolol to slow her heart rate. Twenty minutes later, her headache is worse, and her blood pressure is 238/132 mm Hg. Plasma free metanephrines are later found to be markedly high, and CT shows a 5-cm right adrenal mass. Which mechanism best explains the rise in her blood pressure after propranolol?
choices: Direct stimulation of vascular alpha-1 receptors by propranolol
Blockade of presynaptic alpha-2 receptors with more norepinephrine release
Loss of beta-2 vasodilation, leaving alpha-1 vasoconstriction unopposed
Increased renin release from juxtaglomerular cells after beta blockade
Inhibition of norepinephrine reuptake into sympathetic nerve endings
questions.explanation: The tumor releases large amounts of catecholamines. **Beta-2** receptors in skeletal muscle arterioles normally cause some vasodilation that partly balances **alpha-1** vasoconstriction. A nonselective **beta-blocker** removes this balance, so alpha-1 vasoconstriction is **unopposed** and blood pressure rises sharply; this is why alpha-blockade must come first. Propranolol does not act on alpha receptors, and beta-blockers **lower** renin release, because juxtaglomerular renin secretion is stimulated through beta-1 receptors.
questions.explanation_pt: O tumor libera grandes quantidades de catecolaminas. Os receptores **beta-2** das arteríolas do músculo esquelético normalmente causam alguma vasodilatação, que equilibra em parte a vasoconstrição **alfa-1**. Um **betabloqueador** não seletivo remove esse equilíbrio, a vasoconstrição alfa-1 fica **sem oposição** e a pressão arterial sobe muito; por isso o bloqueio alfa deve vir primeiro. O propranolol não age nos receptores alfa, e os betabloqueadores **reduzem** a liberação de renina, pois a secreção de renina pelas células justaglomerulares é estimulada por receptores beta-1.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has had 3 weeks of fast, jerky, chaotic eye movements in all directions, sudden jerks of his arms and an unsteady walk. He is irritable but alert. Blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg. A firm, irregular mass is felt in the left upper abdomen and extends past the midline. Urine homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid are high. MRI of the brain is normal. Biopsy of the mass shows small, round blue cells around central cores of fibrillar material. Which mechanism best explains his neurologic findings?
choices: Spread of tumor cells to the cerebellum and brainstem
Tumor growth through the neural foramina that compresses the spinal cord
Catecholamine excess acting directly on brainstem neurons
An immune response to tumor antigens that cross-reacts with neurons
Hyponatremia from tumor-related ADH secretion
questions.explanation: This child has **neuroblastoma** (an abdominal mass that crosses the midline, high **HVA/VMA**, small round blue cells in rosettes) with **opsoclonus-myoclonus** syndrome. This is a **paraneoplastic** disorder: the immune response against the tumor also attacks neurons, mainly in the cerebellum and brainstem. A normal brain MRI argues against metastases, which rarely involve the brain in neuroblastoma. Spinal cord compression causes leg weakness and bladder problems, not chaotic eye movements.
questions.explanation_pt: Esta criança tem **neuroblastoma** (massa abdominal que cruza a linha média, **HVA/VMA** altos, pequenas células redondas e azuis em rosetas) com síndrome de **opsoclonia-mioclonia** (*opsoclonus-myoclonus*). É um distúrbio **paraneoplásico**: a resposta imune contra o tumor também ataca neurônios, principalmente no cerebelo e no tronco encefálico. A RM de crânio normal fala contra metástases, que raramente acometem o encéfalo no neuroblastoma. A compressão medular causa fraqueza nas pernas e alterações vesicais, e não movimentos oculares caóticos.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with HIV infection has taken antiretroviral therapy that includes ritonavir for 6 months. He has used inhaled fluticasone for asthma for several years. Over 4 months, he has gained weight around the abdomen, and his face has become round. He bruises easily. Blood pressure is 150/94 mm Hg. Exam shows wide purple striae on the abdomen and thin skin. Fasting glucose is 138 mg/dL. His 8 AM serum cortisol is low, and plasma ACTH is low. Which mechanism best explains his condition?
choices: Reduced hepatic CYP3A4 breakdown of the inhaled glucocorticoid
Ectopic ACTH production by an HIV-associated lymphoma
Fat redistribution caused directly by protease inhibitor therapy
Cytomegalovirus infection destroying the adrenal cortex
Higher cortisol-binding globulin levels induced by ritonavir
questions.explanation: **Ritonavir** strongly inhibits **CYP3A4**, the enzyme that clears **fluticasone**. The inhaled steroid builds up in the blood and causes **iatrogenic Cushing syndrome**; it also suppresses CRH and ACTH, so the patient's own **cortisol is low** (fluticasone is not measured by the cortisol assay). Protease inhibitor lipodystrophy can cause central fat and a dorsal fat pad, but it does not cause purple striae, easy bruising or a suppressed ACTH and cortisol. Ectopic ACTH would raise ACTH and cortisol, and CMV adrenalitis would lower cortisol but raise ACTH, without Cushing features.
questions.explanation_pt: O **ritonavir** inibe fortemente a **CYP3A4**, enzima que elimina a **fluticasona**. O corticoide inalado se acumula no sangue e causa **síndrome de Cushing iatrogênica**; ele também suprime o CRH e o ACTH, e por isso o **cortisol** do próprio paciente fica **baixo** (a fluticasona não é medida pelo ensaio de cortisol). A lipodistrofia dos inibidores de protease pode causar gordura central e coxim dorsal, mas não causa estrias violáceas, facilidade para formar equimoses nem supressão de ACTH e cortisol. O ACTH ectópico elevaria o ACTH e o cortisol, e a adrenalite por CMV reduziria o cortisol, mas elevaria o ACTH, sem sinais de Cushing.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman was diagnosed with autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency 2 months ago and started oral hydrocortisone. Her energy and appetite are better, but she still feels dizzy when she stands up, and she craves salty food. Blood pressure is 104/66 mm Hg lying down and 88/58 mm Hg standing. Her skin is less dark than before. Serum sodium is 132 mEq/L, potassium is 5.4 mEq/L, and plasma renin activity is markedly high. Which drug should be added to her treatment?
choices: Dexamethasone
Desmopressin
Fludrocortisone
Methylprednisolone
Midodrine
questions.explanation: In **primary** adrenal insufficiency the **zona glomerulosa** is also destroyed, so she lacks **aldosterone** as well as cortisol. Orthostatic hypotension, salt craving, **hyperkalemia** and a **high renin** show that the mineralocorticoid deficit is not corrected. **Fludrocortisone** is a potent mineralocorticoid receptor agonist and replaces aldosterone. Dexamethasone and methylprednisolone add glucocorticoid effect with little or no mineralocorticoid effect, and midodrine only raises vascular tone without correcting the sodium and potassium problem.
questions.explanation_pt: Na insuficiência adrenal **primária** a **zona glomerulosa** também é destruída, e falta **aldosterona** além do cortisol. Hipotensão ortostática, avidez por sal, **hipercalemia** e **renina alta** mostram que o déficit mineralocorticoide não foi corrigido. A **fludrocortisona** é um potente agonista do receptor mineralocorticoide e substitui a aldosterona. Dexametasona e metilprednisolona acrescentam efeito glicocorticoide com pouco ou nenhum efeito mineralocorticoide, e a midodrina só aumenta o tônus vascular, sem corrigir o problema de sódio e potássio.
